place: pantropical, Amazonia, Central Africa, Southeast Asia
data: Landsat Analysis Ready Data, compared with Global Forest Change and Tropical Moist Forest
method: Normalized Burn Ratio time series with forest-based local standardization
validation: two-level validation with spatial intersections and temporal stratification, against global datasets
finding: The new Landsat method gave lower bias and root-mean-square error in annual deforestation than widely used global datasets, with the clearest gain in the Congo Basin.
gap_quote: Despite the availability of several global forest change datasets, estimates of annual deforested area differ widely.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Kongo Central, Kasangulu territory
method: mixed methods with remote sensing, household surveys and qualitative interviews
finding: Miombo woodland lost 33 per cent of its area from 2000 to 2025, and charcoal production caused about 60 per cent of the deforestation.

place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Indonesia, Peru
data: Landsat 5 and 7 Thematic Mapper, MODIS Vegetation Continuous Fields, Landsat VCF
method: maximum likelihood classification and MODIS VCF guided forest and non-forest masking
validation: 500 validation pixels at each study area
measures: overall accuracy highest for forest and non-forest masking, values not stated
finding: Masking guided by MODIS VCF had the highest overall accuracy and labelled change best, and Landsat VCF overestimated forest cover in all three areas.
gap_quote: it was found that Landsat VCF substantially underestimates non-forested land cover and as a result overestimates forested land cover in all study areas.

data: land use change matrix of intact forest land, non-intact forest land and other land
method: matrix approach with a bookkeeping carbon model, sensitivity analysis and Monte Carlo simulation
predictors: time interval, forest carbon stocks, carbon increment, edge width, resolution, treatment of fallows
measures: sensitivity of fluxes 4.2 per cent to 262.2 per cent of the reference emission level
finding: The record released the land use change matrix and results for Panama, 1992 to 2000. Modelling sources of uncertainty caused the largest error in reference level emissions.
gap_quote: Substantial technical challenges hinder precise and accurate estimation of forest-related emissions and removals, as well as the setting and assessment of reference levels.

data: GLanCE and GLC_FCS30D land cover products
method: analysis of land cover class change within radii of 1 to 30 km, homogeneity tests and machine learning anomaly detection
predictors: land cover class proportions near the station
finding: Land cover change around 62 Polish stations was analysed with two Landsat products, and its effect on measurements was assessed for one stationary and one relocated station.

place: Amazon Basin, Brazil Jamanxim National Forest, Bolivia Amboro and Carrasco National Parks, Peru Tambopata and Bahuaja-Sonene
method: land use change models integrating quantitative analysis with conservation discourses
predictors: slope, population density, surrounding non-forest, distance to agriculture, fires, legal threats, payments for ecosystem services projects, REDD+ projects
validation: model performance compared with standard land use change models
finding: Integrated models outperformed standard models. Deforestation rose near farms, fires and forest fragments, and some commonly cited factors such as REDD+ projects were not supported.
gap_quote: Standard, quantitative approaches to land-use change (LUC) modeling may omit some factors, constraining understandings of and responses to deforestation.

place: pantropical, including Gulf of Guinea, Atlantic Forest, Southeast Asia, Madagascar
method: spatially explicit GIS analysis with a meta-analysis of ecosystem service studies
predictors: agricultural rent, carbon stocks, ecosystem service values
finding: Externalities of tropical deforestation exceeded agricultural benefits nearly everywhere, and conversion appeared economically efficient only in the Atlantic Forest, around the Gulf of Guinea and in Thailand.
gap_quote: Much of this deforestation occurs with a lack of information on the spatial distribution of benefits and costs of deforestation.

data: satellite images of different periods, GPS data, field observations and surveys
method: GIS mapping of urban front development
finding: The study mapped informal urban growth on risk prone land in north west Yaounde, including uncontrolled deforestation, for use in decision making.
gap_quote: Urban disorder and land use abuse marked by uncontrolled deforestation, wetland occupation and soil degradation for settlement, agriculture and commerce is high in the newly occupied zones necessitating research and measures to pre-empt future disaster in this area.

method: integrated report on forests within development
measures: almost 2 million hectares of tropical forest lost each year
finding: Almost 2 million hectares of tropical forest were lost each year in West and Central Africa, and the report set out policy responses and the role of the World Bank.
gap_quote: If we do not begin to halt the destruction of these forests in the near future, it may become too late to preserve them.

place: Lake Tanganyika catchment, Burundi, Zaire, Tanzania
data: remote sensing rainfall estimates, ARTEMIS NDVI archive, FEWS rainfall archive
method: regional soil erosion model with sediment routing and sediment delivery ratio
predictors: rainfall, vegetation cover, deforestation and land degradation scenarios
validation: remote sensing rainfall compared with kriged raingauge data
finding: Three catchment regions were highly sensitive to erosion. Deforestation was almost total in Burundi, with high sediment entering the north of the lake.
